title: The Battle Is NOT Your’s But God’s, So Give Your Fight To God (Christian Motivation)
paragraphs: We're all familiar with battles. From personal struggles, temptations, societal pressures, challenges in relationships, finances, and health, we constantly find ourselves facing different obstacles. Sometimes we may even wonder why certain challenges seem so overwhelming. But you know what? We're not going to let these battles define us or deter us. Instead, we'll lean into our faith, trust in God's plan, and rise stronger than before. Give your fight to God.

Today, I want to remind you that you are not alone in your battles. Every challenge, every struggle, every tear that you shed has a purpose in God's divine plan for your life. The trials you face are but temporary. They won't last forever. In the midst of it all, remember that God's unwavering love and strength are your anchor, guiding you through even the stormiest of seas. I'm also going to pray a powerful prayer with you in the mighty name of Jesus.

So, watch until the end and open your hearts to receive the blessings of this prayer. Second Chronicles 20 verse 15 reads, "Thus says the Lord to you, do not be afraid nor dismayed because of this great multitude, for the battle is not yours, but God's." The scripture confirms that the battle is not yours, but the Lord's. Also, consider this whenever you are faced with battles.

Ephesians 6 verse 12, "For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. The word of God makes it clear that our fight is much deeper than the physical. There is also a spiritual aspect to our battles. When confronted with these battles, our natural inclination is to rely on ourselves. Yet, this self-reliance often leads us down paths filled with obstacles.

Fear and anxiety sneak into our hearts, attempting to our faith. In our desperation, we may seek worldly solutions, unintentionally bypassing the divine interventions waiting for us. So, let's look at eight key truths to know when facing battles. Truth number one, God's strength surpasses ours. Imagine you're in a tug-of-war, straining against a force you can't seem to overcome. This is what it feels like when we rely solely on our strength.

Isaiah 40:29 gently reminds us, "He gives power to the weak and to those who have no might. He increases strength." We have limitations, but God's power is limitless. When we acknowledge our limitations and invite God into our battles, we tap into a strength that surpasses understanding. Let's revisit the story of Moses at the Red Sea. The Israelites, having just escaped from Egypt, found themselves trapped between Pharaoh's approaching army and the vast Red Sea. The situation seemed hopeless.

They couldn't see a way out, and fear began to grip their hearts. Yet, Moses proclaimed, "Do not be afraid. Stand still and see the salvation of the Lord." And what happened next was nothing short of a miracle. The mighty sea parted, creating a path for the Israelites, showcasing God's supreme power over nature in seemingly impossible circumstances. In parallel, the scripture that was just read from Isaiah 40:29 offers us a similar promise.

It's as if we're being reminded that just like the Israelites at the Red Sea, we're not alone in our struggles. Our energy might wane, our resolve might falter, and at times the way forward may seem blocked. Yet, God's power is unwavering. He can make a way for us where there seemed to be no way. So, whenever we're cornered by life's challenges, feeling overwhelmed and outnumbered, let's remember the Red Sea moment.

By acknowledging our limitations and genuinely inviting God into our battles, we experience a divine intervention. God's strength takes over, making paths where none existed, and granting us victories that seemed out of reach. In him, our battles are not just manageable. They are conquerable. Truth number two, battles have purpose. Life is often a complex web of events that might seem haphazard or even purposeless. But, have you ever wondered why you face certain battles?

James 1:2-4 "My brethren, count it all joy when you fall into various trials, knowing that the testing of your faith produces patience. But, let patience have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing." It's a reminder that our battles can serve a divine intent. Reflect on Joseph's life. Betrayed by his brothers, sold into slavery, falsely accused, and imprisoned. Each trial, each battle, seemed to push him away from his dreams.

But in hindsight, these very battles positioned him for his destiny to be a savior during famine. Through his journey, Joseph could declare, "You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good." Every challenge we face is refining our character, molding us, and drawing us closer to God. It might not make sense now, but with faith and patience, we'll see the purpose in every battle. Yet, this truth isn't exclusive to Joseph alone.

Throughout scriptures, countless individuals faced insurmountable odds, enduring periods of suffering and questioning, only to be led to a divine revelation. Take for example, the story of Ruth, a Moabite woman. She faced heartbreak early in life with the death of her husband. Her decision to follow her mother-in-law, Naomi, leaving her homeland and everything familiar, could be seen as a journey into more uncertainty.

Yet, her unwavering loyalty and steadfastness led her to Boaz, setting the stage for her to become the great-grandmother and an ancestor of Jesus Christ. Her battles, her challenges, and her decisions were all integral parts of God's divine purpose. This perspective shifts our understanding of battles. No longer should they be seen as just mere disruptions or inconveniences. They become platforms for divine revelation and transformation.

They act as channels through which God's purpose flows into our lives, further revealing to us aspects of His character and His plans that we might have otherwise missed. So, when we find ourselves amidst a storm, instead of asking why me, let's start asking, "What are you teaching me, Lord?" For in the heart of that battle lies a purpose, a lesson, and a divine strategy waiting to unfold. Truth number three. Our role is obedience. God's role is outcome. Imagine planting a seed.

Once it's in the ground, you trust it to grow. You don't dig it up to check. Similarly, our battles demand a level of trust. Proverbs 3:5-6 whisper to our hearts, "Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding." This scripture beckons us to act in obedience and leave the results to God. When Noah was instructed to build an ark, he didn't see rain. He might have even seemed foolish to those around him. Yet, his focus was unwavering. His trust was absolute.

He obeyed, and God honored that obedience. We might not always understand God's methods, but our role is to trust and obey while leaving the outcome in God's capable hands. Look at Abraham, called to sacrifice his only son, Isaac. To the outside world, and perhaps even to his own heart, the command seemed unimaginable. It went against the promise that God had given him about Isaac. Yet, Abraham's obedience was steadfast. Without hesitation, he prepared for the sacrifice.

It was in that ultimate act of surrender and obedience that God provided a ram in the bush, thus sparing Isaac. This profound act of faith demonstrates that even when God's requests may seem beyond our understanding or our emotional capacity, our primary role remains to obey. When we put our complete trust in him, God's divine plan takes shape, ensuring the outcomes align with his perfect will for our lives. Truth number four. Fear not, for God is with us.

Ever walked in a dark alley and felt reassured when someone walked beside you? That's the power of presence. Deuteronomy 31:6 is God's promise of his constant presence. Be strong and of good courage. Do not fear nor be afraid of them. For the Lord your God, he is the one who goes with you. He will not leave you nor forsake you. This reminds me of Daniel, trapped in a den of hungry lions. While the situation looked bleak, God was with him. The lions, ferocious as they were, became harmless.

God's presence transformed a battle into a testament of faith. Whatever battle you face, remember this, you are not alone. With God by your side, fear has no place. Similarly, in the life of Moses, there were numerous occasions where fear could easily have overtaken him. Standing before the Pharaoh, leading a nation through a desert, or even encountering God in the burning bush, yet at each crossroad, God's assurance was clear, "I am with you."

It's not the absence of challenges that makes us fearless, but the overwhelming awareness of God's unyielding presence. Every moment we feel surrounded by uncertainties, the echoing promise is that God is greater than all our fears combined. The ocean's depth is intimidating until you realize the one who walks on its waves is with you, guiding you through every storm. Truth number five. Take steps to hand over your battles to God.

In the midst of life's turbulence, there's a profound sense of peace when we choose to release the reins of control and fully trust in God's sovereignty. Surrendering doesn't mean giving up, but rather it signifies embracing a greater power at work. Proverbs 3 verses 5 to 6 directs us, "Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding. In all your ways, acknowledge him, and he shall direct your paths."

Prayer, meditation, and delving deep into the scriptures are essential pathways through which we can offer our battles to the Lord. In these sacred moments, our spirits intertwine with his, and we are rejuvenated, reminded of his steadfast love and the promises that awaits us. Further, the Holy Spirit acts as our steadfast guide, leading us when we're unsure, comforting us when we're downtrodden, and enlightening us when we're in the dark. Romans 8:26 affirms, "Likewise, the Spirit also helps in our weaknesses.

For we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the Spirit himself makes intercession for us in every challenge, every uncertainty, every moment we feel overwhelmed, there lies an opportunity to lean on the Holy Spirit, to immerse ourselves in God's word, and to fortify our faith. When we make the conscious choice to hand over our battles, God transforms them into triumphant testimonies of His glory. Drawing nearer to God and handing over our battles requires a daily commitment.

The act of letting go and entrusting our worries to God can be a daunting task, especially when we're accustomed to being in control. Yet, 1 Peter 5 verse 7 compassionately instructs us to cast all your care upon Him, for He cares for you. By actively immersing ourselves in prayer, meditating on His word, and seeking the counsel of the Holy Spirit, we begin to foster a deep-rooted trust. This trust transforms our perspective, converting our fears into faith.

With each day and each battle handed over, we witness the transformative power of God in our lives, solidifying our belief that He is indeed in control, continuously working behind the scenes for our ultimate good. Truth. Number six. The victory is preordained. Have you ever rewatched a movie knowing the end, but still getting engrossed in the story? Our battles with God are much the same. 1 Corinthians 15 verse 57 exclaims, "But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ."

Joshua and the Israelites stood before Jericho, a city with fortified walls. They were instructed to march around the city, a strategy that seemed strange. Yet, victory was already assured. The walls crumbled. Not by might, but by obedience and trust in God's promise. Our battles might seem insurmountable, but with God, the victory is already preordained. Reflecting again on the Exodus story, the Israelites found themselves trapped between the Egyptian army and the Red Sea. To the natural eye, there was no way out.

No hope for deliverance. But God had a plan, a preordained victory. As Moses stretched out his staff, the seas parted providing a way where there seemed to be none. When the Egyptians pursued, the waters returned ensuring God's people was safe. What appeared to be a dire situation was part of a divine strategy to showcase God's power in our lives, even when the odds are against us, and escape routes seem nonexistent. Remember that God's preordained plan is in motion.

His victories are not bound by what our eyes can see or our minds can comprehend. Truth number seven. God equips us for every battle. Let's think about the exam aspect of school for a moment. Every exam requires specific tools, pens, pencils, rulers, and so on. You have to be equipped in life's battles. God ensures we're equipped. In the book of Ephesians 6:10-11, the scripture advises, "Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord and in the power of his might.

Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. Esther, a queen, was equipped not with weapons, but with wisdom, courage, and divine favor to save her people. God provides what we need for our battles, whether it's wisdom, patience, courage, or resilience. We just need to put on the armor he provides. Look again at the story of Moses. Raised in Pharaoh's palace, he was educated in all the knowledge of Egypt.

Yet, when God called him to lead the Israelites out of Egypt, Moses doubted his ability to speak and lead. He saw his shortcomings, but God saw his potential. God equipped Moses with his staff, which became a symbol of power throughout the journey. More importantly, God gave Moses his brother, Aaron, to speak on his behalf. Every tool, every helper, every circumstance was arranged by God to ensure Moses was prepared for the challenges ahead.

Similarly, we need to trust that God has already provided us with everything we need for the battles we face, whether seen or unseen, tangible or intangible, our tools are divinely purposed for victory and truth. Number eight. We fight from a place of victory, not for victory. It's exhilarating to start a race ahead of everyone else. Colossians 2:15 reveals, "Having disarmed the powers and authorities, he made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them by the cross."

Moses, instructed by God, raised a bronze serpent in the desert. Those bitten by snakes only had to look upon it to be healed. The battle against the venom was won the moment they set their eyes on the bronze serpent. Similarly, Christ's victory on the cross means our battles are already won. We aren't striving to win, but proclaiming the victory already achieved in Jesus. Many of us often feel like we're starting from behind, hustling just to catch up. Yet, the gospel offers a refreshing perspective.

We begin from a position of triumph, just as an athlete trains, not wondering if they will win, but to claim a victory they foresee. We too approach life's challenges from a standpoint of anticipated success. Think of the walls of Jericho, which seemed invincible. Yet, for the Israelites, the victory was certain, even before they began their first march around the city. Their actions weren't to achieve victory, but to claim what God had already promised.

In the same way, when we face struggles and obstacles, we should be uplifted by the assurance that in Christ, the ultimate triumph is already ours. We don't wrestle in desperation, but in confident affirmation of the victory Christ already secured. Friends, as we reflect on these spiritual battles, let's remember they aren't ours, but God's. Today, think about the battles you're facing. Lay them at the foot of the cross. Lay down your weapons. Lay down your fears. And rest assured in his victory.

If God is for us, who can stand against us? In every trial, we have the assurance of victory through God. These eight truths are foundational. By embracing them, we can navigate life's challenges with faith, hope, and confidence. Let them be the pillars that uphold you in every battle. Remember, with God on your side, every battle leads to a testimony of his goodness and grace. Now, to all those within the sound of my voice, let us go to the Lord in prayer.

I want you to pray this prayer with me, so that you can have all the blessings of this prayer. Let us pray to our gracious and loving God, heavenly Father, almighty, and everlasting God, the creator of the heavens and the earth. You, oh Lord, are the alpha and omega, and your praises will forever be on my lips. Forgive me, Lord, for the times I have faulted, for the sins I've committed knowingly and unknowingly. Lord, cleanse me from all unrighteousness and make me whole.

In the mighty name of Jesus, I declare that every battle I face is already won. I declare that every Goliath and wall of Jericho that is standing before me shall fall and crumble. For you, oh Lord, have already given me the victory. In the name of Jesus, I rebuke every spirit of fear and doubt that tries to attack my mind and spirit. I plead the blood of Jesus over my life, ensuring I walk in confidence, rooted in the victories of the cross.

Father, as I navigate the storms of life, thank you for reminding me that my role is to obey, while yours is to to the outcome. Lord, help me to clothe myself daily in your full armor so I may stand firm against the enemy's tactics. Heal me, Lord emotionally, physically and spiritually. Let your divine protection be my shield and may your blessings overflow in abundance in my life. Lord God, I lift up my loved ones to you. I ask that you bless them, protect them and guide them in every decision they make.

May they, too, come to recognize the divine purpose in every battle and understand that with you the victory is already theirs. Lord, as I say this prayer together with everyone listening, I am grateful for each heart that is opening to you right now. For those who are weary, may you renew their strength. For those who are doubtful, may you help to solidify their faith. For those feeling defeated, may you remind them of the victories ahead.

For those who feel alone, may the presence of your Holy Spirit comfort and surround them with the warmth of your love. Lord, for those battling sickness, emotional and mental issues and addictions, may you grant them healing, strength, deliverance and peace of mind that surpasses all understanding. Father, we submit every area of our lives to you as we declare that the battle is not ours, but yours. May you help us to align our thoughts, desires and actions with your divine will.
